questions.question: Guru Har Rai Ji was which Guru in the line of the ten Sikh Gurus?
questions.explanation: Guru Har Rai Ji was the seventh Sikh Guru, succeeding his grandfather Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Har Rai, Guru

questions.question: Guru Har Rai Ji was the grandson of which Guru?
questions.explanation: Guru Har Rai Ji was the grandson of Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji, who chose him as successor.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Har Rai, Guru

questions.question: Who was the father of Guru Har Rai Ji?
questions.explanation: Guru Har Rai Ji's father was Baba Gurditta, the eldest son of Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Har Rai, Guru

questions.question: Which town in present-day Ropar district was the seat of Guru Har Rai Ji?
questions.explanation: Guru Har Rai Ji was born at Kiratpur Sahib and kept his seat there throughout his Guruship.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Har Rai, Guru

questions.question: According to tradition, how many horsemen (armed cavalry) did Guru Har Rai Ji maintain?
questions.explanation: Guru Har Rai Ji kept a force of 2,200 armed horsemen, continuing Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji's tradition, though he never fought a battle.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Har Rai, Guru

questions.question: In a well-known childhood episode, what deeply moved young Har Rai Ji to tears?
options: His robe brushed against a flower and broke it
A bird fell from its nest
questions.explanation: As a boy, Har Rai Ji's flowing robe knocked a flower off its stem in the garden, and he was moved to tears out of compassion.
questions.source: Basics of Sikhi: Guru Har Rai Ji

questions.question: After the flower episode, who advised young Har Rai Ji to gather up his robe when walking so as not to harm anything?
questions.explanation: Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji advised him to hold his robe carefully, teaching that one's actions should cause no harm.
questions.source: SikhNet: Guru Har Rai Sahib

questions.question: Guru Har Rai Ji sent rare herbal medicine to cure which Mughal prince?
questions.explanation: When Dara Shikoh fell gravely ill and the royal physicians failed, Guru Har Rai Ji sent medicine from his herbal stores, and the prince recovered.
questions.source: SikhNet: Guru Har Rai Sahib

questions.question: Dara Shikoh, whom Guru Har Rai Ji helped, was the eldest son of which emperor?
questions.explanation: Dara Shikoh was the eldest son of Emperor Shah Jahan; he later lost the war of succession to his brother Aurangzeb.
questions.source: SikhNet: Guru Har Rai Sahib

questions.question: Guru Har Rai Ji set up a dispensary at Kiratpur. What did it provide?
options: Free medicine and treatment for the sick and poor
questions.explanation: Guru Har Rai Ji ran a dispensary that gave free medicine and care to the sick and needy, regardless of who they were.
questions.source: Sikh Missionary Society UK: Guru Har Rai

questions.question: Which Mughal emperor summoned Guru Har Rai Ji to Delhi?
questions.explanation: Aurangzeb summoned Guru Har Rai Ji to Delhi after reports that he had helped Dara Shikoh and that the Sikh scripture was critical of Islam.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Har Rai, Guru

questions.question: Whom did Guru Har Rai Ji send to Aurangzeb's court in his place?
questions.explanation: Guru Har Rai Ji declined to go himself and sent his elder son Ram Rai to the Mughal court.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Har Rai, Guru

questions.question: To please Aurangzeb, Ram Rai altered the Gurbani phrase "Mitti Musalman ki". What word did he substitute for "Musalman"?
questions.explanation: Ram Rai changed the line to "Mitti Beiman ki" (the clay of the faithless); Guru Har Rai Ji refused to forgive this alteration of Gurbani.
questions.source: Sikh Missionary Society UK: Guru Har Rai

questions.question: The line Ram Rai altered at Aurangzeb's court was the composition of which Guru?
questions.explanation: The line comes from Guru Nanak Dev Ji's Asa di Var; Guru Har Rai Ji rebuked Ram Rai for altering Guru Nanak's words.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Har Rai, Guru

questions.question: Where did Ram Rai settle after being rejected by Guru Har Rai Ji, having received land from Aurangzeb?
questions.explanation: Ram Rai withdrew to the Doon valley, where the town of Dehradun grew around his dera.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Har Rai, Guru

questions.question: When pressed to reconsider Ram Rai, Guru Har Rai Ji compared the Guruship to what?
options: A lamp that must never go out
A river that flows only one way
Tiger's milk that only a golden cup can hold
A sword that must stay sheathed
questions.explanation: He said Guruship is like tiger's milk, which only a golden vessel can hold, and declined to see Ram Rai again.
questions.source: Sikh Missionary Society UK: Guru Har Rai

questions.question: Whom did Guru Har Rai Ji name as his successor?
questions.explanation: Guru Har Rai Ji passed the Guruship to his younger son, Guru Har Krishan Ji, before his passing at Kiratpur in 1661.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Har Rai, Guru

questions.question: Where did Dara Shikoh come to meet Guru Har Rai Ji in 1658 after losing the Battle of Samugarh?
questions.explanation: After his defeat at Samugarh in May 1658, Dara Shikoh met Guru Har Rai Ji at Goindval while fleeing Aurangzeb.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Har Rai, Guru

questions.question: How did Guru Har Rai Ji's horsemen help the fleeing Dara Shikoh?
options: They took control of the boats at the Beas river, delaying Aurangzeb's army
They hid him in Kiratpur fort
questions.explanation: Guru Har Rai Ji's cavalry secured the boats on the Beas, delaying the pursuing Mughal army so Dara Shikoh could escape.
questions.source: SikhNet: Guru Har Rai Sahib

questions.question: Guru Har Rai Ji blessed the boy Phul, whose descendants ruled which princely states?
questions.explanation: Guru Har Rai Ji blessed Phul that his descendants would rule; the Phulkian states of Patiala, Nabha and Jind descended from him.
questions.source: SikhNet: Guru Har Rai Sahib
